title: β-Caryophyllene transcriptomics across HepG2 and hypoxic UFH-001: a descriptive count-model comparison
question: Which metabolic and signaling responses to terpene exposure are reproducible, and which depend on cellular context or a specific target?

claims.text: The UFH-001 source has one shared three-library DMSO control group and 20 µM and 200 µM β-caryophyllene arms under hypoxia; the independent HepG2 study used different culture and exposure conditions.
claims.limitation: Cell identity, oxygen, dose, time, and vehicle are confounded across studies.

claims.text: The receipt-pinned count-model comparison joins 12,453 genes tested in both studies by versioned gene ID. The HepG2 contrast has 1,343 BH-FDR < 0.05 genes in this common universe; UFH-001 has 0 at 20 µM and 121 at 200 µM.
claims.limitation: The contrast significance counts depend on within-study sample size, dispersion, and exposure; their difference is not a formal interaction test.

claims.text: At 200 µM in UFH-001, 31 genes meet BH-FDR < 0.05 in both studies: 12 have matching fold-change signs and 19 have opposite signs. Across all common tested genes, Spearman fold-change correlations are -0.016 at 20 µM and -0.049 at 200 µM.
claims.limitation: These descriptive comparisons do not establish reproducibility of a pathway, a cellular-context interaction, or target specificity.

claims.text: Run a matched factorial study in both cell lines with shared vehicle, oxygen, exposure time, dose and viability controls, biological replicates, and HMGCR or PGF perturbations; prespecify pathway and interaction tests.
claims.limitation: Target attribution also needs genetic rescue or orthogonal binding and functional evidence.
